what: The catch-delay study, written and committed before it is run: on the 24 real catches (results/real_catches_v1.json), how long after the file appeared in the pull request did a maintainer object to it? Itemator asks when the pipeline finishes, so this is the wait a person's own catch took. A description of 24 public cases, not a rate and not a saving.
unit: one case of results/real_catches_v1.json: one file on one public agent pull request that a human reviewer objected to
start: the later of the pull request's created_at and the committer date of the first commit in the pull request whose file list contains the path (GitHub API, GET only). A reviewer cannot see a file before both.
end: the case's comment_created_at (the reviewer's objection), as already recorded in results/real_catches_v1.json
primary_outcome: the median of end minus start over readable cases, with the minimum and maximum
secondary: cases where the objection came within one hour, and cases where it came one day or more after the start
the same median by outcome (file_removed, closed_unmerged, landed_with_the_file)
unreadable: a case is unreadable when the API does not return the pull request, its commits or a commit holding the path (for example a force-push removed it); it is counted and reported, never guessed
sentence: On the {n} files reviewers objected to, the objection came a median of {median} after the file appeared in the pull request ({within_hour} within an hour, {day_or_more} a day or more later). Itemator's card asks when the pipeline finishes.
which_sentence: the one sentence, filled in and used word for word in docs/measurements.md, whatever it says
we_never: claim the reviewer would have caught it sooner with Itemator, or that the whole wait is time lost
change start or end after the run starts
runs_in: eval/catch_delay.py, locally, about 24 pull requests and their commits through `gh api` (GET only); no Duo credits
